knowledge:
- key_parameters: rowLevel=A vector of node IDs (leaves and internal nodes) to aggregate counts for in aggTSE ;; rowFun=The function used to aggregate counts (e.g., sum) in aggTSE ;; option=The differential analysis method to run (e.g., "glmQL" for edgeR QLF) ;; filter_min_total_count=The minimum total count threshold to filter out lowly abundant nodes ;; threshold=The threshold parameter t used in getCand to propose aggregation candidates ;; limit_rej=The FDR significance threshold (e.g., 0.05) used in evalCand ;; type=The evaluation type in evalCand ("multiple" for DS analysis across multiple features) ;; use_pseudo_leaf=Logical indicating whether to use pseudo leaves during candidate evaluation
- alternatives: The documentation notes that any differential abundance or state method can be used instead of the built-in runDA/runDS wrappers, provided it outputs a data frame containing node numbers, p-values, and effect size signs.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing entities structured hierarchically (e.g., microbial species in a phylogenetic tree, cell subpopulations in a clustering tree) where differences between conditions may occur at varying levels of resolution (individual leaves or aggregated subtrees).
- pitfalls: Blindly aggregating across the entire tree can lose the ability to pinpoint specific highly resolved features with strong signals. Lowly abundant nodes must be filtered out to avoid low-power tests. Multiple nodes having the same label can trigger warnings during aggregation.

workflows.name: differential_abundance_analysis
workflows.intent: Find entities or subtrees whose abundance is associated with a sample phenotype.
input: da_lse (TreeSummarizedExperiment object containing feature counts, sample metadata, and a row tree representing hierarchical relationships among features)
workflows.stages: 1. Get all node IDs using showNode ;; 2. Aggregate counts for internal nodes using aggTSE ;; 3. Perform differential abundance analysis for leaves and nodes using runDA ;; 4. Extract node results using nodeResult ;; 5. Propose aggregation candidates using getCand ;; 6. Evaluate candidates to find the optimal aggregation level using evalCand ;; 7. Summarize candidates using infoCand and extract significant nodes using topNodes ;; 8. Evaluate performance using fdr and tpr
workflows.code:
all_node <- showNode(tree = rowTree(da_lse), only.leaf = FALSE)
da_tse <- aggTSE(x = da_lse, rowLevel = all_node, rowFun = sum)
da_res <- runDA(da_tse, assay = "counts", option = "glmQL", 
                design = model.matrix(~ group, data = colData(da_tse)), 
                contrast = c(0, 1), filter_min_count = 0, 
                filter_min_prop = 0, filter_min_total_count = 15)
da_tbl <- nodeResult(da_res, n = Inf, type = "DA")
da_cand <- getCand(tree = rowTree(da_tse), score_data = da_tbl, 
                   node_column = "node", p_column = "PValue",
                   threshold = 0.05, sign_column = "logFC", message = FALSE)
da_best <- evalCand(tree = rowTree(da_tse), levels = da_cand$candidate_list, 
                    score_data = da_tbl, node_column = "node",
                    p_column = "PValue", sign_column = "logFC")
infoCand(object = da_best)
da_out <- topNodes(object = da_best, n = Inf, p_value = 0.05)
fdr(rowTree(da_tse), truth = rownames(da_lse)[rowData(da_lse)$Signal], 
    found = da_out$node, only.leaf = TRUE)
tpr(rowTree(da_tse), truth = rownames(da_lse)[rowData(da_lse)$Signal], 
    found = da_out$node, only.leaf = TRUE)

workflows.name: differential_state_analysis
workflows.intent: Find genes that are differentially expressed between conditions in either a single cell subpopulation or a group of similar subpopulations.
input: ds_tse (TreeSummarizedExperiment object containing single-cell count data, cell-level metadata, and a column tree representing hierarchical relationships among cell clusters)
workflows.stages: 1. Aggregate counts to generate pseudobulk samples for each node and sample using aggDS ;; 2. Perform differential state analysis for leaves and nodes using runDS ;; 3. Extract node results using nodeResult ;; 4. Split results by feature and find candidates for each gene separately using getCand ;; 5. Evaluate candidates across multiple features using evalCand with type = "multiple" ;; 6. Extract top significant nodes per feature using topNodes
workflows.code:
ds_se <- aggDS(TSE = ds_tse, assay = "counts", sample_id = "sample_id", 
               group_id = "group", cluster_id = "cluster_id", FUN = sum)
ds_res <- runDS(SE = ds_se, tree = colTree(ds_tse), option = "glmQL", 
                design = model.matrix(~ group, data = colData(ds_se)), 
                contrast = c(0, 1), filter_min_count = 0, 
                filter_min_total_count = 1, filter_min_prop = 0, min_cells = 5, 
                group_column = "group", message = FALSE)
ds_tbl <- nodeResult(ds_res, type = "DS", n = Inf)
ds_tbl_list <- split(ds_tbl, f = ds_tbl$feature)
ds_cand_list <- lapply(seq_along(ds_tbl_list), 
                       FUN = function(x) {
                           getCand(
                               tree = colTree(ds_tse),
                               t = seq(from = 0.05, to = 1, by = 0.05),
                               score_data = ds_tbl_list[[x]], 
                               node_column = "node", 
                               p_column = "PValue", 
                               sign_column = "logFC",
                               message = FALSE)$candidate_list
                       })
names(ds_cand_list) <- names(ds_tbl_list)
ds_best <- evalCand(tree = colTree(ds_tse), type = "multiple", 
                    levels = ds_cand_list, score_data = ds_tbl_list, 
                    node_column = "node", 
                    p_column = "PValue", 
                    sign_column = "logFC", 
                    feature_column = "feature",
                    limit_rej = 0.05,
                    message = FALSE,
                    use_pseudo_leaf = FALSE)
ds_out <- topNodes(object = ds_best, n = Inf, p_value = 0.05)
